_comment: The HopLobby submission form, field by field (see 03-Resources/hoplobby-developer-docs/11-submission-and-review.md). Also the arguments for the HopLobby MCP prepare_submission call, which saves a DRAFT only; the user presses Submit on the portal. Drop this _comment key before sending.
title: Battle Drones
tagline: Fly a stealth drone and hunt target drones that roll, dodge and shoot back. Up to 8 pilots, 3 courses, 3 bosses.
description:
Battle Drones is a three-minute drone hunt for 1 to 8 pilots. You play as your own HopLobby avatar: walk out to your launch pad, throw your stealth drone into the air by hand, pull the goggles on and fly it in first person.

The host picks the course in Match settings: City, Mountain, Dunes or Random. City is a run between towers, billboards and rooftops. Mountain is a snowed-in valley with a high col, a gorge and light snowfall. Dunes is open desert with pyramids, obelisks to thread, ruined columns and an oasis.

Every pilot chases their own pack of 60 target drones along the course. They flee, weave, barrel-roll out of the way of your shots and fire back. A normal target is worth 1 point; every tenth is a tougher gold ace worth 3. Forty seconds in, the course's boss arrives with a swarm of small one-hit drones: the Big Tech CEO over the city, Evil Santa in his sleigh drone on the mountain, the Mummy Pharaoh in a flying sarcophagus in the dunes. Bring a boss down for 15 points; he comes back later for another go. Most points when the clock runs out wins, and ties go to whoever got there first.

You have 100 health. Enemy fire, buildings, trees, lampposts and hard landings all cost you; get shot down and you are back in three seconds with a short shield. A barrel roll or a flip dodges incoming fire, and an obstacle sensor warns you about what is ahead.

Everyone gets the same targets and the same boss, so the round is fair, and everything fast happens on your own machine, so there is no lag in your shots. You see the other pilots' drones and a live scoreboard as you fly.

Controls: arrows or WASD fly, Space fires, Q and E barrel roll, X flips, Shift brakes, C swaps between first person and a chase camera, O toggles the obstacle sensor, I inverts climb, M toggles sound. A standard controller works too: left stick flies, right trigger fires, left trigger brakes, bumpers roll, Y flips. Steering eases in smoothly, and Steering sensitivity (Gentle, Smooth, Normal, Twitchy), invert climb, camera and the obstacle sensor are all in HopLobby's Esc menu.
notes: No server of our own; nothing is saved (no leaderboards, achievements, store). Host pattern: the host sends one start message (course, seed, pilots); each player then runs their own copy of the round, so shots and hits are local and lag-free. The relay carries only drone positions and scores, 10 per second per player. Scores are self-reported, a deliberate trade for a casual game with no saved results. Incoming messages are validated and dropped if malformed (tools/net-test.js, 17 checks: junk, reload, leaver, host leaving). Late join supported. No asset files: models, textures and sounds are built in code (no AI-generated image, model or audio files; the code was written with the help of Claude Code, an AI coding assistant). three.js r158 (MIT) bundled. localStorage holds two settings. Keyboard or controller; no touch yet. English and pt-PT. Bosses and billboard brands are original, no real people or companies. Source: public GitHub repo, hoplobby.json at root (build.output Work). Update 2026-11-16: smoother steering (eased turn rate + stick response curve, from player feedback); SDK 1.7.0 (unchanged copy); course is now a lobby option (no own picker); the host ends each round with endGame(results) (no own play-again loop; HopLobby reloads per round, no session flag); follows HopLobby.graphics presets (pixel ratio, draw distance, debris and snow particles; auto step-down only on Auto); settings and key list in HopLobby.menu.set().
